messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 — Sudden KV cache + continuous-batching regression detected. Memory per-host spiking 5-15x and tail latency cliffing for several clusters. Paging oncall: @Shreya (oncall). See runbook: https://runbooks.internal/kv-cache-frag

Shreya (oncall): On it. Which clusters are impacted? any customer-facing errors?

Diego: impact map in grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/KV/kv-cache?orgId=1&var-cluster=all — north-america-prod-1, eu-west-prod-2 show the biggest growth. OOMs in cuda malloc logs on a subset of nodes.

Morgan: Confirmed elevated 95/99 latencies in userdata-route and chat-route. Spike started ~10:13 UTC.

Beth (CS): I already heard from Acme Health and one other mid-market customer — they see degraded responses and timeouts. They've escalated to TAM.

Jules (TAM): forwarding customer logs, they have an SLA window open. Need ETA on mitigation.

Diego: Early triage — looks like new batching heuristics we rolled last night increased prefix KV lifetime and prevented compaction, leading to allocator fragmentation. We're seeing many small KV allocations and arena churn leading to high fragmentation and eventual cuda malloc failures.

Shreya (oncall): Can we throttle batching or revert the config quickly?

Diego: Yes. Plan A: revert batching config to previous commit and restart inference pools on impacted clusters. Plan B: if restart risky, apply temporary batch size caps via env override.

Shreya (oncall): Execute Plan B immediately on na-prod-1 as a quick mitigation. Who can push the change?

Morgan: I'll do the env override and scale up nodes if needed. Applying to na-prod-1 now:

```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/redwood-runtime CONTBATCH_MAX_ITEMS=8 CONTBATCH_PREFIX_TTL=60
```

Morgan: Pushing... :hourglass_flowing_sand:

eng-runtime-bot: Patch applied to na-prod-1: CONTBATCH_MAX_ITEMS=8, CONTBATCH_PREFIX_TTL=60 (deployed by Morgan).

Diego: Good — that should reduce in-flight KV growth. Also kicking off a selective compaction job against affected arenas (non-disruptive).

Shreya (oncall): Monitoring. Please report CPU/memory and tail latency over next 10m.

Morgan: Memory trend flattening on na-prod-1 — 10% drop after env change. Latency 95% improving slowly.

eng-runtime-bot: Canary rollout of config revert (commit abc122 -> abc121) started on eu-west-prod-2 (5/50 nodes). Logs: `rollout/abc121 started`

Diego: If canary looks good, we'll continue rollouts. Revert includes: batching heuristic disable + arena tuning patches that reduce fragmentation.

Beth (CS): Customer update ready — telling Acme Health we have a mitigation in place and are rolling a config revert, will follow up in 30m.

Kai: Heads-up from product — are we rolling back a feature? Need notes for release and postmortem. Also - are any A/B experiments affected?

Diego: Yes rollback of the heuristic part only. We keep telemetry on to compare. No A/B other than the nightly rollout.

Morgan: Canary looks good. Continuing revert rollout across clusters. Commands used for restart (safe restart):

```
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/redwood-runtime --selector=pool=kv-optimized
```

Shreya (oncall): We're seeing reduced OOMs and fragmentation metrics trending down. Nice work.

eng-runtime-bot: Revert rollout completed on all impacted clusters (na-prod-1, eu-west-prod-2, apac-prod-1).

Diego: Next steps: 1) run an offline compaction+defrag sweep on nodes that still show high internal fragmentation, 2) roll forward with a safer batching experiment and lower default limits, 3) add telemetry alert for sharp KV allocation growth.

Jules (TAM): Acme Health acknowledged the update and paused SLA escalation for now. They want a follow-up within 24h.

Beth (CS): I'll schedule the customer follow-up and postmortem summary.

Shreya (oncall): Summary for channel: mitigation applied (env cap + config revert), rolling restarts, OOMs reduced, customer impacted but notified. Owning the oncall bridge until further notice.

Diego: Assigning postmortem owners: Diego (root cause analysis), Morgan (operational mitigations + runbook updates), Kai (product + release notes), Beth/Jules (customer comms).

Shreya (oncall): Add follow-up actions to oncall board and link to triage doc: https://notes.internal/kv-batch-cliff-triage-26153

Morgan: small playbook note: add a fast rollback knob for batching heuristics and a read-only compaction run for emergency use.

Diego: Also will add a preflight regression test for batch heuristics on a synthetic workload to catch allocation growth.

Kai: Please tag me in the postmortem draft. Need timeline for release-safe re-landing.

Shreya (oncall): I'll leave the bridge to Diego for deeper RCA. Oncall clear for now but will monitor for 2 hours. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident P0 transitioned to "mitigated" at 2615301500. Postmortem required.

Diego: Noting one additional follow-up — investigate if torch/pytorch allocator flags (PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_POOL) change behavior; we saw subtle differences under fragmentation.

Beth (CS): I'll prepare customer-facing summary and share internal postmortem link when ready.

Shreya (oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing slack bridge in 30m unless new alerts. :thumbsup:
